prompt:
Create ONE finished 16:10 horizontal game concept frame by selectively repainting the two people in the supplied original “Threshold” image. This art direction intentionally assigns DIFFERENT levels of modeling to characters and background. Use the supplied image as the authoritative reference for the BACKGROUND and composition.

BACKGROUND: retain the original's broad, restrained, opaque color shapes almost exactly. Preserve the ash slope on the left, off-register towering wall slabs cropped above the top edge, violet-black walkable gate in the middle, narrow reflection on the worn sill and one corridor bend disappearing into darkness. Match the existing gray-violet/blue-gray/earth-ochre palette, matte painted shapes, sparse detail, shoulder-height camera and light arrangement. Keep the faint existing paper character. Do not pencil-shade the background, model every stone, add architecture, or spray new texture over it.

CHARACTERS — the important visible change: replace both stylized, angular, flattened figure renderings with genuinely more lifelike, dimensional, artist-modeled adult people, of the same identities and costumes. Render like two believable hand-painted character maquettes in an illustrated game scene. Use anatomically convincing shoulders, elbows, wrists, hips, knees and load-bearing ankles. Give the faces a true eye socket, eyelid thickness, a nose that turns into the light, cheekbone, jaw and soft transitions through multiple halftones. Lips, tired gaze and compression of a fingertip communicate more than surface detail. Hair groups and fabric folds should have rounded volume. Reserve subtle sharper local edges for eyes, knuckles and the contact with the paper. These two human figures should read clearly more modeled than their surroundings in a thumbnail. Restrained hand-painted surfaces, natural proportions, no photographic skin pores, camera bokeh, plastic figurine gloss, all-over pencil marks, dark ink contours, graphic hatching, or polygon facets on flesh.

On the left the lean young ADULT survivor in a short faded ochre jacket, scarf and work trousers pauses in three-quarter profile at the threshold. Their forward leg takes the weight and the other rests back, head lowered in exhaustion. The near hand gently turns a small limp provision pouch mouth-down, just a few grains of ash falling out. Fingers pinch the fabric, the wrist and forearm visibly carry the small weight; the other arm hangs slack. On the right the older, heavy-shouldered bald gatekeeper sits low behind his knee-high rough table. His broad sleeve hangs from a naturally supported elbow; his heavy lids are directed toward the cards. Show his near hand clearly, index and middle finger softly flexed, pads flattening one corner of a single cream card on a small clean cloth. Remaining fingers at ease. The farther hand steadies the cloth without hiding the three separate cards and their simple faded doorway motif. Keep the shaded lantern at the far right. Both people share the SAME cool skylight, gray-violet reflected shadows, and correct grounding on the ash floor. Amber lamp warms the gatekeeper's nearest fingers and card; a little of that warm bounce may reach his lowered cheek. Feet, stool, table and card corners have small grounded contact shadows to integrate the different treatments. It must feel like ONE unified hand-painted storytelling scene, not two photographic cutouts over an illustration. No text, no UI, no signatures, no split views.
